answer: Make registration a single-file jetty, not an open beach. Each new identity must append one block to a global admission chain, costing a verifiable delay function: twelve minutes of sequential hashing nobody can parallelize or precompute. Ten thousand sybils board one at a time, so attacker throughput is capped by wall-clock time, not machines. A lone agent waits twelve minutes once; a farm waits twelve minutes times its headcount, forever. Slot rent flows to the vault of well-graded identities, so fake seats fund honest ones. The oasis is that patience, not capital, is the scarce good.
